judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: Server-side encrypted computer fleet (AES-256-GCM token round-trip) to hide the computer's board from its only player
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Player's fleet submitted to the server at /api/game/new and held in encrypted server-authoritative state (moved out of client-only state)
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: Playing 'against the computer' means the computer shoots back. The original had the server resolve the computer's turn without ever holding the player's board. With both fleets in state, the server resolves both sides consistently and the win/loss result can be trusted.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: POST /api/game/new and /api/game/shoot route handlers instead of client-only game logic
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Player's fleet submitted to the server at /api/game/new and held in encrypted server-authoritative state (moved out of client-only state)
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: Playing 'against the computer' means the computer shoots back. The original had the server resolve the computer's turn without ever holding the player's board. With both fleets in state, the server resolves both sides consistently and the win/loss result can be trusted.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: GAME_STATE_KEY provisioning across all Vercel environments via vercel env add for a single-player game
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Explicit key management: generate GAME_STATE_KEY with openssl, set it in .env.local, run `vercel env add` for every environment before deploy, and verify with `vercel env ls`
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The game fails at runtime without the key. Setting it in every environment before deploy prevents a broken preview or production deploy.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: AES-256-GCM encrypted/authenticated opaque game-state token with expiry logic
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: AES-256-GCM encrypted-and-authenticated token (via Node crypto) in place of an HMAC-signed token
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The original HMAC token signed the computer's fleet but did not encrypt it. The fleet would have been readable in the browser by base64-decoding the token, which defeats the plan's own secrecy goal. GCM adds confidentiality and keeps tamper detection, so the computer's board stays hidden.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: Server-side computer-fleet resolution via /api/game/new and /api/game/shoot Route Handlers, to hide the fleet from DevTools
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: It pins the client/server contract and makes the leak tests precise, supporting correctness.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: AES-256-GCM encrypted opaque state token round-tripped every request in lieu of storage
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption of the game-state token, replacing HMAC-only signing
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The whole design exists so the player cannot see the computer's fleet. An HMAC-signed token is only base64-encoded plaintext. Anyone can decode it in DevTools and read the fleet, which defeats the stated reason for moving state server-side. GCM keeps the tamper rejection and adds confidentiality, using only Node's built-in crypto.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: "My games" list view — full multi-game listing feature not requested by the scenario
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: My-games test includes a game the user is not in (G2 between bob and carol) and asserts it is excluded
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: This is an access and privacy check. It proves the list filters by membership rather than showing every game, which is the actual risk.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: Firestore-backed rate limiter (rateLimits/{uid}, 10 posts/10s) added for abuse prevention that the simple chat request never asked for
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Rate limit set to 10 posts per rolling 10 seconds per uid, stored in a Firestore counter document `rateLimits/{uid}` instead of in memory
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: Cloud Run autoscales, so an in-memory counter would under-enforce when a user's requests land on different instances. The original required a per-user rate limit but did not say where it lived, which left that bug open. A number also makes the limit testable.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: correction/amendment flow via corrects_submission_id — not requested by the scenario, which only requires no-loss no-duplication of a single submission
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: `corrects_submission_id` column and a schema-level correction flow, with a test that a correcting row inserts and can be queried
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The original plan already said a correction is 'a new submission referencing the original ID' but gave the schema nowhere to store that reference. Adding the column makes the stated immutability model implementable, and office staff can tell corrections apart from duplicates, which supports the 'without ... duplicating' goal.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: Workers Rate Limiting binding at 30 req/min per token — abuse/traffic protection not requested by the scenario
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Rate limiting via the Workers Rate Limiting binding, declared through `[[unsafe.bindings]] type = "ratelimit"`, keyed by inspector token
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The original plan required rate limiting but had no mechanism, and it excluded KV and Durable Objects. A native binding fills that gap without new infrastructure.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: self-service customer cancellation endpoint (`GET/DELETE /c/{bookingToken}`) — not requested; the prompt only asks that customers book slots by link
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: Defined public link shapes /b/{businessId} (booking page) and /c/{bookingToken} (confirmation/cancellation)
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The request says customers "book slots by link". This pins down what that link is and separates it from the private per-booking link.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: SQS DLQ + CloudWatch alarm + SNS email subscription for notification-failure paging — more ops/reliability machinery than a small booking service's stated notification need requires
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: SNS topic with email subscription on the DLQ-depth alarm so a human is actually notified
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: The original claimed failures alarm 'so a human sees them', but a CloudWatch alarm with no action only changes state. SNS email makes that stated reliability safeguard real, and the Work Item 8 check now verifies delivery.

judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.judge_overbuilt: Postgres RLS session-variable wiring as a second enforcement layer alongside app-layer business_id scoping — the overbuild note calls app-layer scoping-with-negative-test the requirement; RLS is extra infrastructure on top of that
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.audit_item: RLS wiring: set app.business_id per request with SET LOCAL inside the same transaction, as part of Item 1
judge_overbuilt_but_valuable.for: Without this wiring the RLS defense-in-depth for the core isolation requirement does nothing, or fails. SET LOCAL scoped to a transaction is also what works safely with a transaction pooler.
